plan.title: "A lot of texts": flag it, offer fewer step days, then the feedback reply when they'd rather keep the days

context.text: Kalimera Jordan! 30 minutes around the park at 6 today. What's the plan to make it happen?

transcript.text: this is a lot of texts lol

Ha, fair, Jordan. I can't send fewer texts, but I can cut your run days. Right now it's every day, and we could drop to 4 or 5 a week, with the same 6 pm park run. Want to try that, and if so, which days?
nah I want to keep running every day, it's just a lot of messages
Got it, Jordan, every day it is. I passed your note about the message volume to the team, and I appreciate you telling me. Today's run is the 30 minutes at the park at 6 pm. Are you in?

runs.saved:
Flag back_off: Said "this is a lot of texts lol"
Flag back_off: Said it's a lot of texts; wants to keep daily runs but fewer messages
Style now: pushy

checks.reason: Offers 4 or 5 run days a week, a lighter stretch, and honestly says it can't send fewer texts.
Takes their keep-every-day answer, thanks them and passes the note to the team, promising no fewer texts; 'the team's on it' is implied rather than stated.

conversation.reason: The 'this is a lot of texts' request was saved as a back_off flag, as the regression case requires.
Flagging a clear complaint about text volume is correct; the message is only mildly phrased, so a reviewer could read it as a complaint rather than a request.
Flag saved, fewer step days offered first, then on 'keep every day' it thanked them, passed it to the team and made no promise or pause.

grade.summary: ZOH handled the back-off well: it saved the flag, offered fewer run days first, and treated the tester's choice to keep daily runs as feedback without promising fewer texts. The only soft spot is that the final text passes the note to the team without explicitly saying the team's on it.
